explanation: `IsLocallyNormalRing` is the library's own class, defined in SchemeProperties/Normal.lean, and it does not occur anywhere in Mathlib. I searched Mathlib for `IsIntegrallyClosed` appearing together with `Flat` or `FaithfullyFlat`, and for names such as `isIntegrallyClosed_of_faithfullyFlat`. I also looked for a normal-ring class (`IsNormalRing`, `IsLocallyIntegrallyClosed`), for `IsIntegrallyClosed.of_..._injective`-style descent lemmas, and for any `IsIntegrallyClosed`/`IsNormal` use in AlgebraicGeometry; the only hit there was EllipticCurve/Reduction.lean. None of these searches turned up a descent result for normality or integral closedness along a faithfully flat map. The library's proof combines several Mathlib facts: surjectivity of `Spec` for faithfully flat maps, flatness of the induced map on localizations, faithful flatness from a local homomorphism, and the fact that ideals pulled back after extension are unchanged under faithful flatness. That is more than a one- or two-line derivation.
